newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 1.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 1.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday :

* U.S blue-chip stocks fell on Monday as investment managers adjusted portfolios on the final day of the second quarter, and the bond market slid on strong economic data. The Dow Jones industrial average lost 14.93 points to close at 7,672.79.

* The 1996 slowdown in Asia's economic growth was largely cyclical and is coming to an end and with the omens improving, a broadening recovery could be underway, investment house Lehman Brothers said in a report on Monday.

* Jakarta stocks ended up 1.08 percent on Monday at a record 724.56 points on the back of continuing strong fundamentals in the economy, brokers and analysts said. The index rose 7.73 points during the day.
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,433.00/34.00 at 0150 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,431.80/32.30.
* Medium-sized Bank Bahari BARI.JK on its debut on Tuesday when the bank lists 262 million shares on the Jakarta bourse.

* Property firm PT Dharmala Intiland on a news report on Tuesday that it had an operational cooperation pact with Putra Surya Perkasa to market Dharmala Intiland property projects. The Bisnis Indonesia daily quoted a Dharmala executive as saying the companies had no plans for a merger.
* Property firm Bakrieland on continued market talk that it would be involved in the construction of a mass rapid transportation project, brokers said.

* PT Asiana Multikreasi following a report in the Harian Ekonomi Neraca newspaper on Tuesday that it planned to propose a 10-for-10 rights issue attached with three warrants at a price of 500 rupiah each share.
* Tamara Bank on reports that it had tied up with China Trust Commercial Bank of Taiwan and planned to launch their joint venture bank in Jakarta on July 23.
* Newly listed company PT Asia Inti Selera after it won shareholders approval to pay dividends of 60 rupiah per share.

* Transportation firm Steady Safe on news reports that the city land transportation agency will urge the government to raise the regular city buse fare as it was considered too low, the Jakarta Post reported on Tuesday.
* Blue chip toll-road operator Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada and transportation firm Steady Safe after Steady Safe reportedly said it will buy an 11.01 percent stake in Citra Marga.
* Lippo Securities on reports it has revised up its 1997 net profit forecast to 121.6 billion rupiah from its 95.7 billion rupiah.
* Poultry firm Cipendawa on reports of a proposed 80 billion rupiah rights issue.
* Cigarette maker Sampoerna on reports it is in talks to form an alliance with Indonesia's largest conglomerate, the Salim Group.
